newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 22.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- Support for the return of the present Irish government has increased significantly in the past week, according to the latest opinion poll ahead of the general election on June 6.
- The three government parties will on Thursday unveil a single 600 million Irish pounds package of tax changes for the next two budgets.
- Another Church-State clash over abortion loomed on Wednesday as Ireland's Prime Minister John Bruton unequivocally rejected calls by Dublin's Catholic archbishop for a new referendum on the issue.
- A new wave of selling hit the Irish pound on Wednesday as currency traders again targeted the pound's position in the European currency grid.

- Ireland and other member nations of the EU should ensure that their currencies do not become overvalued against the currencies of trading competitors in the Far East and the U.S., Independent Newspapers chairman Tony O'Reilly said on Wednesday.

- The two main opposition parties, Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats, hold a lead of 12 percentage points over the three government parties in the first Irish Times/MRBI opinion poll conducted since the calling of the general election last week.
- The Irish pound has nosedived again after overseas speculators began targeting the currency for the second time in three weeks.

- Unionists were furious on Wednesday after a warning by Northern Ireland Secretary Mo Mowlam that they could be excluded from the peace process if they opposed entry to talks by Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army.

- Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats have increased their lead over the combined coalition parties in the first opinion poll of the general election campaign, boosting their hopes of winning office on June 6.
- Irish interest rates and the pound came under pressure on Wednesday as the market braced itself for the another possible raid on the currency.
